findings.title: enableSqlExpressions() is dead code that always returns false regardless of input
findings.body: The function computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then has `if enabled { return false }` followed unconditionally by `return false`. Both branches return false, so the computed `enabled` value is never actually used to determine the result — the function always returns false no matter the feature-toggle state. While this currently achieves the intended 'always disable SQL expressions' behavior, the code reads as if it is still gating on the feature flag, which is misleading. A future maintainer (or an automated 'bug fix' from a linter/refactor) could easily 'simplify' this by flipping the dead branch (e.g. to `return true`) believing they're restoring flag-based behavior, silently re-enabling the vulnerable SQL expressions path. The function should be simplified to explicitly `return false` with a comment explaining this is a deliberate, permanent disablement pending further hardening, rather than leaving confusing unreachable logic tied to the feature flag.

findings.title: No test added verifying SQL expressions are blocked regardless of feature toggle state
findings.body: This PR is a security fix meant to permanently disable SQL Expressions (to close an RCE/LFI vulnerability), but no test was added to pkg/expr covering ReadQuery with QueryTypeSQL for both FlagSqlExpressions enabled and disabled, asserting that an error is always returned. Given the severity of the vulnerability being fixed and the confusing logic in enableSqlExpressions, a regression test is necessary to prevent this security control from being accidentally removed or inverted in a future change.

findings.title: Stub DB implementation always errors, likely breaking existing SQL expression tests not updated in this PR
findings.body: The new DB struct's TablesList, RunCommands, and QueryFramesInto methods unconditionally return 'not implemented' errors, replacing the previously functional github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck implementation. If pre-existing tests in pkg/expr (e.g. sql_command_test.go, pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go) assert successful SQL parsing/execution results, they will now fail since every call returns an error instead of a parsed table list or query result. None of these test files appear in the diff, so it is unclear whether they were removed/adjusted; if they still exist unmodified, CI would break.

findings.title: No documentation update reflecting that SQL Expressions are now permanently non-functional
findings.body: The PR description explicitly states the FlagSqlExpressions feature toggle is left untouched and existing docs that only mention the flag's existence are not updated. However, after this change, enabling the toggle has no effect — SQL Expressions will always fail with 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' (and now also always fail internally via the stubbed DB in pkg/expr/sql/db.go). Users/admins who toggle FlagSqlExpressions on, expecting functionality based on existing docs, will be confused by always-failing behavior with no documentation explaining why. At minimum a brief doc or code comment update is warranted to avoid confusion during the period this feature is dead code.
